title: First real impact traces: 12/12 captured, classical recovery is a coin flip, and the speed sweep collapsed
question: What does a real collision look like at 200 Hz (pitch/rate/yaw/wheels/duty), and how often does the classical balancer recover from it -- the anchor data for fitting sim contacts before training the speed-chaser policy?
headline: All 12 segments captured a hit (zero voids; self-calibrated rate triggers landed at 260-390 deg/s, 3-5x the old fixed 80 floor -- vindicating calibration over quiet-hold). Head-on signature: wheels 850->0 deg/s in ~90 ms, pitch whips to ~300 deg/s and ~24 deg excursion, recovery slams full reverse. Classical recovery: 5/12 falls. The 45-deg glancing hit (seg 11) reads clearly as the left wheel decaying 190 ms before the right, with roughly half the peak rate and pitch of head-on. BUT the speed sweep collapsed: cruise duty limit-cycles rail-to-rail at ~9 Hz and mean wheel speed sits at 640-890 deg/s regardless of the 300-750 target -- the classical law cannot track cruise speed on this floor, so all impacts landed at ~0.27-0.38 m/s. Speed control is itself an open problem the policy has to solve.
hub_output: gains: 10.71 0.87 0.43 0.3 tau: 30 slew: 150 trig: rate> 80 or stall< 0.5
